CO2016A-P1-61.exp: A note attached to a cell pops up on hover and is known as a cell tip (the cell comment). Smart tips and the other two are not Excel terms.

CO2016A-P1-62.exp: Every Excel formula must begin with the equals sign, which is what tells Excel to evaluate what follows instead of storing it as text. Entering the operators and values (option C) is the step that comes after the = has been typed, so it cannot be first.

CO2016A-P1-63.exp: The formula bar, just above the column headings, is where the active cell's value or formula is typed and edited. The title bar shows the file name and the toolbars hold commands, so neither accepts data.

CO2016A-P1-64.exp: You add first and round the single result: =ROUND(SUM(D4:D17),0), where 0 decimal places gives a whole number. ROUND requires that second argument, so option C is incomplete, and wrapping ROUND around a whole range inside SUM (B and D) is invalid syntax.

CO2016A-P1-65.exp: The Currency Style button on the formatting toolbar applies the $#,##0.00 number format in one click, changing only how the value is displayed. The underlying number stays 1000, which is why retyping the data is never necessary; there is no Format > Money command.

CO2016A-P1-66.exp: Dollar signs before both the column letter and the row number, $A$1, lock the reference so it does not shift when the formula is copied. Plain A1 is relative, and the ! and # forms are not Excel syntax at all.

CO2016A-P1-67.exp: When Excel creates a defined name from a label, the label and its value must sit adjacent in the same row or the same column — Create from Selection reads labels from the top row, bottom row, left column or right column. Restricting it to only a row or only a column would be too narrow, and a single cell cannot hold both label and value.

CO2016A-P1-68.exp: Excel's What-If Analysis menu contains exactly three tools: Scenario Manager, Data Table and Goal Seek. 'Target', 'Prediction' and 'Future Value' are not entries on that menu (FV is a financial function, a different thing).

CO2016A-P1-69.exp: A design template supplies a ready-made colour scheme, fonts and background graphics that can be applied to a new presentation. The master slide is where you edit those elements yourself, and an animation scheme controls motion rather than look.

CO2016A-P1-70.exp: Animation Scheme is the PowerPoint feature that applies ready-made motion effects to the objects on a slide; slide transition governs the move between slides, not objects within one, and 'Animation Objects' is not a real command. In current PowerPoint versions the equivalent lives on the Animations tab (and finer per-object control is the Animation Pane), so the 2003-era name is dated.

CO2016A-P1-71.exp: Ctrl+M inserts a new slide in the open presentation. Ctrl+N creates a whole new presentation file and Ctrl+S saves, so 'All of above' is clearly wrong.

CO2016A-P1-72.exp: Rehearse Timings runs the show while recording how long you spend on each slide, then offers to save those timings for automatic playback. The other three names do not exist in PowerPoint.

CO2016A-P1-73.exp: Grouping combines several objects into one so that moving, resizing or formatting acts on all of them together and preserves their relative positions. Aligning and positioning are separate commands and are not what grouping itself does.

CO2016A-P1-74.exp: PowerPoint slides default to landscape orientation, since slides are meant to be projected on a wide screen. Portrait is available but must be selected in Page Setup; grid and tile are not orientations.

CO2016A-P1-75.exp: Slide Sorter view shows thumbnails of every slide at once, which is how you rearrange or delete slides in bulk. Slide Show runs the presentation full screen one slide at a time, so it does not let you see them all together.
